To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the most-selectivity detection of 15 PAHs was possible when GC–MS APPhCI with benzene as gas reagent was used.
the fast and selective detection of 16 selected PAHs was possible in a 44-compound mixture using GC-MS AP-PCI with toluene as a gas reagent.
the use of GC-MS APChI and APPhI with vapors of benzene and toluene allows the selective detection of 16 of the 44 components of the mixture.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of a fast, sensitive, and selective method for the detection of PAHs in complex mixtures of organic compounds.
the development of the fast and selective detection of 16 priority PAHs in the complex mixtures of organic compounds.
the development of a fast method for the selective determination of 16 PAHCs in the complex mixture of organic compounds using the GC-MS with the use of APPhCI.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the APPhCI GC-MS is a highly-selective and sensitive method for the detection of 16 priority polycyclic aromatic compounds in complex mixtures.
the use of the GC–MS APPhCI technique is the most effective method for the selective detection of 16 EPA-PAHs.
APPhCI is a promising method for the selective detection and identification of PAHs in the complex mixtures of semi-volatile organic substances.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of APPhCI GC-MS is a very effective and selective method of detection for PAHs in the presence of other compounds in a complex mixture.
the use of APPhCI and APPhI with the GC-MS system allowed us to detect PAHs in mixtures of 44 semi volatile organic compounds.
the use of APPhI and GC-MS APPI in combination with GC-MS APPHCI allows the selective detection of PAHs in the presence of other organic compounds in a mixture.
The main takeaway from our work is that
APPhCI GC-MS is the most selective and sensitive technique to detect PAHs in mixtures of organic compounds.
the APPhCI technique is the most suitable method for the detection of polycyclic aromatic compounds in complex mixtures of organic compounds.
the use of the APPhCI technique allows for the fast detection of PAHs in complex mixtures of organic compounds.
